text:
jason: FYI customer (acme) reports EU traffic suddenly landing in us-east since ~07:30 UTC. Huge tail latency (600-900ms) and a spike in 401 auth errors. Customer example request-id: req_0a9f. They say ISP is Vodafone NL.

maria_support: Thanks — pasted their response headers and trace they sent. shows x-region: us-east-1 and geoip-country: US in our edge logs for multiple requests.

maria_support: Example headers they copied:
```
x-request-id: req_0a9f
x-region: us-east-1
via: 1.1 varnish
user-agent: acme-client/2.3
```

suresh_ops: I'm pulling edge logs now. I can see the resolver IPs in front are from an ISP resolver (89.212.45.3). GeoIP lookup for that IP returns country=US in our current DB.

ingrid_sre: interesting — that resolver IP maps to an ISP anycast pool. ISP-level caches sometimes return stale edns-client-subnet or wrong geoip mapping. can we run a direct dig from one of their resolvers?

ingrid_sre: quick repro I ran from a probe:
```
dig @89.212.45.3 A edge.redwood.net +short
-> 54.230.12.4  (us-east)
```

tim_runtime: this matches our fallback routing policy: if geoip lookup doesn't map to a supported EU region we fall back to us-east to avoid capacity mismatches. that logic is intentional but causes cross-continent routing when geoip is wrong.

maria_support: Customer asks for an immediate workaround — can they force EU region via header?

tim_runtime: for hosted we accept an opt-in hint header `x-region-hint: eu-west-1`, but only for customers with region-pinning enabled. we can temporarily enable a per-customer hint for acme; will need a quick config flip.

suresh_ops: short-term steps: 1) ask ACME to switch to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 to test if resolver changes mapping, 2) provide region-hint header as interim, 3) I'll push a hot GeoIP DB refresh and mark it high priority.

ingrid_sre: long-term: add logic to treat ISP resolver ASNs with known anycast pools as "ambiguous" and prefer continent-level fallback instead of forcing us-east. i'll open an eng-sre ticket.

maria_support: I told the customer the workaround and asked them to run `dig +short @their-resolver edge.redwood.net` and paste results. also asked them to try 8.8.8.8 as a test. they're trying now. :hourglass:

deploy-bot: geoip-db: hotfix deploy started by suresh_ops (job #4521).

suresh_ops: pushed DB refresh and invalidated our in-memory cache on edges. also lowered our fallback-to-us-east threshold temporarily to prefer EU when continent ambiguous. monitoring for errors.

maria_support: Customer confirmed reduced latency after we applied region-hint and after they tested with 8.8.8.8. They still saw a couple of 401s but much better.

ingrid_sre: created INC-2030-0842 to track AS-level exceptions and routing policy change; assigning to tim_runtime for rollout plan.

jason: Thanks team — keeping this thread open until INC-2030-0842 has a mitigation plan and we confirm with ACME that ISP resolved cache. :thumbsup:
